comparison: Take a coefficient estimate constructed from auxiliary dataset B and define the fitted propensity by sigmoid(x dot gamma-hat). This supplies the logistic form, not a particular training algorithm: the source calls l1-penalized logistic regression its numerical default rather than a mandatory theorem construction. Preserve training on B and the resulting independence relations furnished by the separate sampling setup. Positivity of sigmoid for finite arguments does not establish a uniform estimated-overlap margin, coefficient accuracy or denominator moment bounds, and no clipping operation is inserted.

The scalar formula matches; neither component requires penalized fitting or establishes estimated overlap.

comparison: Use Filtration on the fixed ambient measurable space for the increasing information fields, and represent the model as a set of probability laws and each hypothesis as a subset of that model. The unknown actual law belongs to that fixed model; the phrase abstract or not completely known does not define random hypotheses or random measurable spaces. Preserve almost-sure statements separately under every law. This quantifier order does not create a universal null set across laws or across an uncountable family of subsets. Source positive-integer indexing can be represented by positive naturals or an explicit index shift, without silently assigning a hypothesis to zero. The filtration constructor does not itself impose adaptation or an error rate on tests.
gap: Filtration and sets of probability laws express the setup; simultaneous-version conventions for uncountable families remain a separate source issue.

The filtration fields are exactly increasing sub-sigma-algebras; the law and hypothesis sets require no new primitive but do not settle common-null-set questions.

comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i02-p0817/D10: Represent p_i as an [0,1]-valued adapted variable and, for each law in its individual null H_i, bound the CDF of its pushforward law by x for every x in [0,1]. This includes the endpoints as printed. Adapted requires measurability at the current information field, and marginal null validity does not imply conditional superuniformity given the past, mutual independence of p-values, or validity of every intersection-test construction without its separate assumption. Pushforward measurability must be established rather than using its total fallback.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i05-p2241/D3: For the nonnegative variable X, impose the null CDF bound at every alpha in (0,1), and equality at all those thresholds under every null for exactness. For each alternative Q require the reversed weak inequality at all thresholds and a strict inequality at some threshold which may depend on Q. Do not exchange the for-each-Q and exists-alpha quantifiers or reduce power to improvement at a single common threshold. Truncation at one leaves events {X<=alpha} unchanged for the stated open threshold range. This member carries no filtration-adaptation condition from the online-paper variant.

comparison: Use a sequence of binary-valued decisions adapted to the given filtration. Adapted states precisely that d_i is measurable with respect to F_i, so it permits dependence on information available at time i rather than requiring measurability at F_(i-1). The value one denotes rejection and zero the source's acceptance convention. It is a decision representation only: no familywise-error or false-discovery-rate guarantee, independent p-values, conditional null validity or stopping-time property is part of this definition.

comparison: Intersect the hypothesis subsets over the subtype of indices belonging to I, retaining arbitrary infinite I as well as finite I. Use the model of possible laws as the ambient type so the empty intersection is the whole model. The source separately fixes the empty-index test to zero; that test convention does not follow from the intersection constructor. Each phi_I is a measurable binary random variable with one meaning rejection, but this bare definition does not impose a level bound or online measurability at an endpoint. Forming uncountable minima or requiring simultaneous almost-sure comparisons among all such tests needs additional measurability/version reasoning and is not guaranteed by their individual measurability.
